title: NotebookLM guide for small business owners
description: How to use NotebookLM (now Gemini Notebook) to question your own contracts, handbooks and quotes, create audio summaries and keep your documents safe.
author: Cross Tech Edu
cover_alt: A business owner using NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook) to ask questions about PDF documents and listen to an audio summary
body:
**NotebookLM** is Google's free AI tool for **reading and answering questions about your own documents**: contracts, staff handbooks, catalogues, quotes. In July 2026 Google renamed NotebookLM **Gemini Notebook**; it works the same way and lives at the same address. This guide uses both names, since many people still search for NotebookLM.

This NotebookLM guide is for non-technical small business owners: your first notebook in 5 minutes, 5 practical uses in a shop or small company, audio summaries (including in Vietnamese), the limits of the free plan, and privacy.

## 1. How NotebookLM differs from ChatGPT and Gemini

ChatGPT and Gemini answer from general knowledge. NotebookLM is different: **it answers only from the documents you give it**, and adds numbered citations you can click to see the exact passage.

Think of it as **a new employee who reads very fast**: you hand over a stack of documents, they read everything, then answer your questions about that stack and point to the page and line.

That makes NotebookLM a good fit for:

- Finding one clause in a 30-page contract.
- Answering staff questions from your handbook and policies.
- Comparing quotes and catalogues from several suppliers.

It is **not** the right tool for creative marketing copy or questions your documents don't cover. Use ChatGPT or Gemini for those.

## 2. Your first notebook in 5 minutes

All you need is a Google (Gmail) account.

1. On a computer, go to **notebooklm.google** (notebooklm.google.com also works). On a phone, install the app whose developer is **Google LLC**; depending on the version it is called NotebookLM or Gemini Notebook.
2. Sign in and **create a new notebook**.
3. **Add sources:** upload PDFs, pick files from Google Drive (Docs, Slides), paste a website or YouTube link, or paste text directly.
4. Wait a few seconds while it reads. Then type questions in the chat box as you would in any messaging app.

> **Tip:** keep **one notebook per topic**: one for "Shop lease", one for "Staff handbook", one for "Supplier quotes". Mixing unrelated documents makes answers less accurate.

## 3. Answers with citations: how to check them

Each answer has **small numbers** after its points. Hover over or tap a number and NotebookLM opens the exact passage in the original document.

Make a habit of **checking at least one citation** for anything important (money, deadlines, responsibilities). NotebookLM makes things up far less often than a general assistant, but it can still misread a long sentence or miss an exception.

You can also untick sources in the left-hand panel to ask about just one or two documents.

## 4. 5 ways to use NotebookLM in a small business

### A staff assistant built on your handbook

Upload your house rules, opening checklist and returns policy. A new hire asks *"A customer wants to return something after 10 days. What do I do?"* and gets an answer with citations. You can **share the notebook** with staff by their Gmail address, just like a Google Doc.

### Comparing supplier quotes

Upload three PDF quotes and ask:

```text
Make a comparison table of these quotes: unit price, minimum order,
delivery time and payment terms. Point out any terms that are
unfavourable to the buyer.
```

### Reading a contract before you sign

Upload a lease or distribution agreement and ask:

```text
List all fees, penalties, termination conditions and the tenant's
obligations. Cite the exact clauses.
```

NotebookLM helps you **know what to ask**, but it is no substitute for a lawyer on a high-value contract.

### Understanding rules from official texts

Instead of reading opinions online, download the official regulation or guidance from a government website, add it as a source and ask in everyday language. The answer sticks to the text and points to the clause.

### Training staff with audio

Turn training documents into an **audio summary** your staff can listen to on the way to work (see the next section).

## 5. Audio, video and mind map summaries

Beyond Q&A, NotebookLM can turn your documents into several kinds of summaries:

- **Audio summaries:** a conversation between two AI hosts discussing your documents. **Many languages are supported, including Vietnamese.** If yours comes out in the wrong language, change the output language in the settings and generate it again.
- **Video summaries:** a narrated slide presentation, handy for introducing a process.
- **Mind maps:** a diagram of the main ideas and how they connect.

You'll find these on the right-hand side of the screen (a separate tab on mobile). They take a few minutes to generate.

> **Note:** audio summaries sound so natural that they are easy to trust. Check numbers, prices and dates against the original before using one for training.

## 6. How far does the free plan go?

According to Google's help pages at the time of writing, a free account gets:

- **100 notebooks**, each with up to **50 sources**.
- Up to about 500,000 words or 200 MB per source, roughly a thick book.
- A daily limit on questions and on audio and video summaries; when you hit it, wait until the next day.

For a shop or small company, **the free plan is usually enough**. Google's paid AI plans raise these limits; consider them only if you keep running out.

## 7. Privacy when uploading documents

Your documents are stored on Google's servers. For personal Gmail accounts, Google says your NotebookLM content is not used to train its AI models **unless you give feedback** (thumbs up or down) on an answer, in which case the related content may be reviewed by people at Google. So:

- **Avoid rating answers** in notebooks that contain internal documents.
- **Remove personal data** before uploading: ID numbers, bank details, customer phone numbers, payroll.
- **Don't upload documents you are obliged to keep confidential** for a partner unless they agree.
- **Review who a notebook is shared with** whenever someone leaves the business.
- **Turn on 2-step verification for Gmail**, since every notebook is tied to that account.

## 8. Where to start

1. **Today:** create a notebook, upload one long document you need to read (a contract or policy), ask 3 questions and check the citations.
2. **This week:** generate an audio summary in your language and listen on the way to work.
3. **At the weekend:** put your shop's handbook and procedures into one notebook and share it with one employee to try.

To see how NotebookLM compares with other tools, read [6 free AI tools for small business owners](/en/blog/free-ai-tools-for-small-business/). For writing messages and posts, see [how to use Google Gemini in a small business](/en/blog/guide-to-using-google-gemini-for-smes/).

*Checked in October 2026. Google is gradually renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook across its apps, so what you see may differ slightly from this guide.*
